* Bill of Materials
** Source

Either get a tarball (=nyxt-<version>-source-with-submodules.tar.xz=) from a
[[https://github.com/atlas-engineer/nyxt/releases][tagged release]], or clone as a git repository:

#+begin_src sh
mkdir -p ~/common-lisp
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/atlas-engineer/nyxt ~/common-lisp/nyxt
#+end_src

If you already have a clone that was made without submodules, fetch them with:

#+begin_src sh
cd ~/common-lisp/nyxt
git submodule update --init --recursive
#+end_src

There are 111 submodules, all living under =./_build=, and they are shallow (see
=shallow = true= in =.gitmodules=).  Populating them is a prerequisite for any
build.

** Common Lisp

Nyxt is written in Common Lisp.  Currently, we only target one of its
implementations - [[http://www.sbcl.org/][SBCL]].

Nyxt also depends on Common Lisp libraries.  These are bundled in the tarball
mentioned above or fetched as Git submodules (under =./_build=).

Note for advanced users: the single source of truth for CL libraries is dictated
by the Git submodules.  Any Nyxt build that deviates from it is considered
unofficial.  See environment variable =NYXT_SUBMODULES= defined in the makefile
to override the default behavior.

** Web renderers

Nyxt is designed to be web engine agnostic so its dependencies vary.

*** WebKitGTK

Using the latest [[https://webkitgtk.org][WebKitGTK]] version is advised for security concerns.  The oldest
version that supports all features is 2.36.

The packages that provide the following shared objects are required:

- libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so
- libgobject-2.0.so
- libgirepository-1.0.so
- libglib-2.0.so
- libgthread-2.0.so
- libgio-2.0.so
- libcairo.so
- libpango-1.0.so
- libpangocairo-1.0.so
- libgdk_pixbuf-2.0.so
- libgdk-3.so
- libgtk-3.so

To improve media stream it is recommended to install =gst-libav= and the
following plugins:

- gst-plugins-bad
- gst-plugins-base
- gst-plugins-good
- gst-plugins-ugly

*** Electron

[[https://www.electronjs.org/][Electron]] is the default renderer (the =NYXT_RENDERER= make variable is set to
=electron=) and only requires
[[https://nodejs.org/][Node.js]] and =npm=; the WebKitGTK shared objects above are not needed.

The Electron runtime is installed by =npm= on demand: =make all= runs
=make -C _build/cl-electron install=, which is simply =npm install= under
=_build/cl-electron=, before any Lisp code is compiled.  This is a fast,
network-dependent step, so a failure here (missing =npm=, no network access, or
an empty =_build/cl-electron= submodule) aborts the build almost immediately.
Set =NODE_SETUP=false= to skip it.

** Other

The packages that provide the following shared objects are required:

- libssl.so.3
- libcrypto.so.3
- libfixposix.so.3
- libsqlite3.so

Additionally, the following packages:

- xclip :: when using X system;
- wl-clipboard :: when using Wayland;
- enchant :: spellchecking (optional).

* Architecture

Nyxt ships as a single executable which is a whole Common Lisp image, not a
core program with the Lisp fixed on disk.  This matters to anyone planning to
modify or extend it: the binary is self-contained, and user Lisp is compiled
at run time by an embedded compiler rather than at build time.

** One Lisp image, compiler included

=make all= invokes =asdf:make :nyxt/electron-application=, which dumps a core
image with `save-lisp-and-die`: the SBCL run-time, the full Lisp compiler,
Nyxt's own source, and all bundled dependencies (the =_build= submodules) are
compiled into the =./nyxt= ELF executable.

Two consequences follow:

- The compiler is embedded so user code can be compiled at run time.  This is
  what makes the extension model work (see the Configuration section of the
  in-browser manual, =source/manual.lisp=) and accounts for most of the
  binary's size (on the order of one hundred megabytes).
- The binary does not need the source tree or =_build= to run.  At start-up,
  =*source-directory*= (=source/configuration.lisp=) is looked for at ASDF's
  system source-directory, then the XDG data directories, then =share/nyxt/=
  relative to the binary.  If none of these contain a =nyxt.asd=, Nyxt logs
  "Nyxt source directory not found" and runs anyway.  A deployed binary in
  =/usr/local/bin/= with no other files works.

** What lives outside the binary

Lisp itself is fully inside the image; three things are not:

- System shared libraries loaded through CFFI: WebKitGTK/GTK, OpenSSL,
  libfixposix, SQLite.  See the [[*Bill of Materials][Bill of Materials]].
- The renderer.  Nyxt is not a web engine: the default Electron renderer is a
  separate Node/Electron program under =_build/cl-electron/=, whose
  =node_modules= (hundreds of megabytes) must be present at run time.  See
  the [[*Electron][Electron]] entry in the Bill of Materials.
- User data: =~/.config/nyxt/= for configuration and
  =~/.local/share/nyxt/extensions/= for Lisp extensions.

** Extending without rebuilding

Because the image embeds the compiler, extension is additive at run time
rather than a recompile:

- =config.lisp= is loaded with =cl:load= at every start-up into the
  =:nyxt-user= package (=source/start.lisp=).  =define-configuration= patches
  the slots of internal classes without touching the sources, and
  =define-command= adds commands.
- Extensions are regular ASDF systems dropped in =*extensions-directory*=
  (=~/.local/share/nyxt/extensions=), discovered automatically through
  =nyxt-source-registry=, and loaded with =(asdf:load-system ...)=.
- Live evaluation is available through =--eval=, =--load=, =--script= and the
  =--remote= REPL (see the Scripting section of the in-browser manual).

The binary is only rebuilt when Nyxt's own source changes.

* Build artifacts

What a build (=make all=) produces, and what must be kept around afterwards:

- =./nyxt= :: the self-contained executable described in the
  [[*Architecture][Architecture]] section.
- =_build/= :: 111 shallow submodule check-outs of the Lisp dependencies.
  Build-time only: their code is compiled into the image and nothing is read
  from them at run time.  Safe to delete after a successful build (but re-run
  =git submodule update --init --recursive= to restore them).
- =_build/cl-electron/node_modules/= :: the Electron renderer host, installed
  by =npm=.  Run-time dependency of the default renderer; keep it, or re-run
  =make -C _build/cl-electron install= to restore it.
- =~/.cache/common-lisp/sbcl-.../= :: the SBCL FASL cache.  User Lisp
  (configuration, extensions, =--eval=) is compiled on demand by the embedded
  compiler and cached here.  Delete it when behavior seems stale.
- =manual.html= :: a static dump of the manual, produced by =make doc= (the
  =nyxt/documentation= system) for offline reading.  The manual itself is
  always available at run time inside the binary.

** AppImage and packaged layout

Official releases ship as an AppImage: a read-only filesystem image mounted at
=$APPDIR=, running the =nyxt= binary from inside it.  It is laid out by the
=nasdf= installer (=nyxt.asd= lines 348-356, =libraries/nasdf/install.lisp=),
so it bundles:

- =usr/bin/nyxt= :: the self-contained Lisp image described in the
  [[*Architecture][Architecture]] section.
- =usr/share/nyxt/= :: a copy of Nyxt's own sources (=source=, =libraries=,
  =nasdf=) so that =*source-directory*= resolves inside the AppImage at run
  time (the binary looks for =share/nyxt/nyxt.asd= relative to itself, see
  =source/configuration.lisp=).
- =usr/share/applications/nyxt.desktop= and
  =usr/share/metainfo/nyxt.metainfo.xml= :: the desktop entry and AppStream
  metadata.
- =usr/share/icons/= :: the scalable =nyxt.svg= and multi-resolution PNG icons
  used by desktop environments.
- The renderer runtime (the Electron host and its =node_modules= for the
  default renderer) and the system CFFI shared libraries that the image
  loads, bundled so that the AppImage is self-contained.

At run time, Nyxt detects the AppImage via the =APPIMAGE_PATH= environment
variable (=appimage-p= in =source/global.lisp=): the in-browser help then
offers an "Install Desktop Shortcut" button, and the =add-desktop-entry=
command (=source/configuration-commands.lisp=) writes a launcher entry into
=~/.local/share/applications/= and copies icons into
=~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/=.

Note that the AppImage assembly itself is done by the release pipeline, not by
the makefile; this checkout only declares the packaged components above.

* Development environment

Lisp favors incremental program development meaning that you make some changes
and compile them.  In other words, there's no need to compile the whole codebase
or even restart the program.

The typical Common Lisp IDE is [[https://github.com/slime/slime][SLIME]] (or its fork [[https://github.com/joaotavora/sly][SLY]]), which requires being
comfortable with Emacs.  Add the snippet below to Emacs' init file.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(setq slime-lisp-implementations
      '((nyxt ("sbcl" "--dynamic-space-size 3072")
              :env ("CL_SOURCE_REGISTRY=~/common-lisp//:~/common-lisp/nyxt/_build//"))))
#+end_src

Start the REPL by issuing =M-- M-x sly RET nyxt RET= and evaluate:

#+begin_src lisp
(asdf:load-system :nyxt/gi-gtk)
(nyxt:start)
#+end_src

Note that:

- [[https://asdf.common-lisp.dev/asdf/Configuring-ASDF-to-find-your-systems.html][ASDF must be configured to find the required systems]];
- =cffi= must be configured to find the required shared objects by setting env
  var =LD_LIBRARY_PATH= or =cffi:*foreign-library-directories*=.

** Tests

It is recommended to restart the Lisp image before and after running the tests
since some of them are stateful:

#+begin_src lisp
(asdf:test-system :nyxt/gi-gtk)
#+end_src

* Installation

Nyxt uses the =Make= build system.  Run =make= to display the documentation or
see the [[../makefile][Makefile]] for more details.

*** Prerequisites

- [[http://www.sbcl.org/][SBCL]] (the only supported Common Lisp implementation);
- =make=;
- [[https://nodejs.org/][Node.js]] and =npm= (only for the default Electron renderer);
- the system packages listed in the [[*Bill of Materials][Bill of Materials]] section, most of which
  apply to the WebKitGTK renderer only.

Examples (package names vary across distributions):

#+begin_src sh
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install sbcl make nodejs npm \
    libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 libfixposix3 libssl3 \
    xclip # or wl-clipboard on Wayland
#+end_src

#+begin_src sh
# Arch Linux (=make= ships with =base-devel=)
sudo pacman -S --needed sbcl nodejs npm \
    webkit2gtk-4.1 openssl libfixposix sqlite \
    xclip # or wl-clipboard on Wayland
#+end_src

Quicklisp is *not* required: all Lisp dependencies are bundled as submodules
under =./_build=, and any build that resolves them through Quicklisp instead is
considered unofficial (see =NYXT_SUBMODULES= in the makefile).

*** Fresh check-out

#+begin_src sh
mkdir -p ~/common-lisp
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/atlas-engineer/nyxt ~/common-lisp/nyxt
cd ~/common-lisp/nyxt
#+end_src

For an existing clone started without submodules (or after an interrupted
checkout):

#+begin_src sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
#+end_src

Populating the submodules is the very first thing to get right: a missing one
typically fails the build before Lisp compilation even starts, with a =make=
"No such file or directory" or an ASDF =MISSING-DEPENDENCY= error.  Empty
directories left over from an interrupted checkout can confuse git; remove them
and re-run the command above:

#+begin_src sh
for d in _build/*/; do [ -d "$d" ] && [ -z "$(ls -A "$d")" ] && rm -rf "$d"; done
git submodule update --init --recursive
#+end_src

*** Building the binary

#+begin_src sh
make all
#+end_src

This generates the =./nyxt= binary with the default (Electron) renderer.  The
first run downloads the Electron runtime via =npm= and compiles every Lisp
dependency under =./_build=, so expect several minutes and several hundred
megabytes of output.  Subsequent runs are incremental: =.lisp= files are
tracked as make dependencies, so only out-of-date ones are recompiled (change a
file and re-run =make all=).

For the WebKitGTK renderer instead:

#+begin_src sh
make all NYXT_RENDERER=gi-gtk
#+end_src

Other targets: =make check= runs the test suite, =make doc= builds the static
documentation, and =make clean= removes the =./nyxt= binary.  Note that the
INSTALL file (shown by =make= / =make help=) mentions =make install=, but no
such top-level target exists in the makefile.

*** Running the tests

#+begin_src sh
make check
#+end_src

It restarts Lisp, loads the =:nyxt= system, and runs the test suite.  Some tests
are stateful, so restart the Lisp image before and after running them (see the
[[*Development environment][Development environment]] section).

*** Troubleshooting

- An *immediate* failure mentioning =electron=: the first step of =make all= is
  =npm install= under =_build/cl-electron=.  This needs =node= and =npm= on the
  =PATH= plus network access, and fails within seconds - before any Common Lisp
  code is touched.

* Contributing

Nyxt is a joint effort and we welcome contributors!  You can find tasks [[https://github.com/atlas-engineer/nyxt/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Agood-first-issue][on our
issue tracker]] to suit your interests and skills.  Please fork the project and
open a pull request (PR) on GitHub to undergo the reviewing process.  Refer to
the [[*Branch management][branch management section]] for more detailed information.

Please resist the temptation of discussing changes without drafting its
implementation.  Currently, we value pragmatism over creativity.

** Help

Feel free to contact us at any point if you need guidance.

- To learn Common Lisp, see [[https://nyxt-browser.com/learn-lisp]];
- [[https://github.com/atlas-engineer/nyxt/issues][Open up an issue on GitHub]];
- Find Nyxt on Libera IRC: =#nyxt=
- [[https://discord.gg/YXCk7gDKgJ][Nyxt's Discord]];

** Commit style

Ensure to isolate commits containing whitespace changes (including indentation)
or code movements as to avoid noise in the diffs.

Regarding commit messages, we follow the convention of prefixing the title with
the basename when there's a single modified file.  For instance, for changes in
=source/mode/blocker.lisp= the commit message would look as per below:

#+begin_example
mode/blocker: Short description of the change

Further explanation.
#+end_example

** Branch management

Nyxt uses the following branches:

- =master= for development;
- =<feature-branches>= for working on particular features;
- =<integer>-series= to backport commits corresponding to specific major
  versions.

Branch off from the target branch and rebase onto it right before merging as to
avoid merge conflicts.

A commit is said to be atomic when it builds and starts Nyxt successfully.  At
times, for the sake of readability, it is wise to break the changes down to
smaller non-atomic commits.  In that case, a merge commit is required (use merge
option =no-ff=).  This guarantees that running =git bisect= with option
=--first-parent= only picks atomic commits, which streamlines the process.

Those with commit access may push trivial changes directly to the target branch.

** Programming conventions

The usual style guides by [[https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/cmsc421/norvig-lisp-style.pdf][Norvig & Pitman's Tutorial on Good Lisp Programming
Style]] and [[https://google.github.io/styleguide/lispguide.xml][Google Common Lisp Style Guide]] are advised.

For symbol naming conventions, see https://www.cliki.net/Naming+conventions.

Some of our conventions include:

- Prefer =first= and =rest= over =car= and =cdr=, respectively.
- Use =define-class= instead of =defclass=.
- Use =nyxt:define-package= for Nyxt-related pacakges.  Notice that it features
  default imports (e.g. =export-always=) and package nicknames (e.g. =alex=,
  =sera=, etc.).  Prefer =uiop:define-package= for general purpose packages.
- Export using =export-always= next to the symbol definition.  This helps
  prevent exports to go out-of-sync, or catch typos.  Unlike =export=,
  =export-always= saves you from surprises upon recompilation.
- When sensible, declaim the function types using =->=.  Note that there is then
  no need to mention the type of the arguments and the return value in the
  docstring.
- Use the =maybe= and =maybe*= types instead of =(or null ...)= and =(or null
  (array * (0)) ...)=, respectively.
- Use the =list-of= type for typed lists.
- Use =funcall*= to not error when function does not exist.
- Prefer classes over structs.
- Classes should be usable with just a =make-instance=.
- Slots classes should be formatted in the following way:
#+begin_src lisp
(slot-name
 slot-value
 ...
 :documentation "Foo.")
#+end_src

When =slot-value= is the only parameter specified then:
#+begin_src lisp
(slot-name slot-value)
#+end_src
- =customize-instance= is reserved for end users.  Use
  =initialize-instance :after= or =slot-unbound= to initialize the slots.
  Set up the rest of the class in =customize-instance :after=.  Bear in mind
  that anything in this last method won't be customizable for the end user.
- Almost all files should be handled via the =nfiles= library.
- =(setf SLOT-WRITER) :after= is reserved for "watchers",
  i.e. handlers that are run whenever the slot is set.  The =:around= method is
  not used by watchers, and thus the watcher may be overridden.
- We use the =%foo%= naming convention for special local variables.
- We suffix predicates with =-p=.  Unlike the usual convention, we always use a
  dash (i.e. =foo-p= over =foop=).
- Prefer the term =url= over =uri=.
- URLs should be of type =quri:uri=.  If you need to manipulate a URL string, call
  it =url-string=. In case the value contains a URL, but is not =quri:url=, use
  =url-designator= and its =url= method to normalize into =quri:uri=.
- Paths should be of type =cl:pathname=.
  Use =uiop:native-namestring= to "send" to OS-facing functions,
  =uiop:ensure-pathname= to "receive" from OS-facing functions or to "trunamize".
- Prefer =handler-bind= over =handler-case=: when running from the REPL, this
  triggers the debugger with a full stacktrace; when running the Nyxt binary,
  all conditions are caught anyway.
- Do not handle the =T= condition, this may break everything.  Handle =error=,
  =serious-condition=, or exceptionally =condition= (for instance if you do not
  control the called code, and some libraries subclass =condition= instead of
  =error=).
- Dummy variables are called =_=.
- Prefer American spelling.
- Construct =define-command= requires a short one-line docstring without
  newlines.
- Name keyword function parameters as follows =&key (var default-value
  var-supplied-p)=.

# - Conversion functions =FROM->TO= or =->TO= for generic functions.  The
#   only one that comes to mind is =url= which does not follow this convention...

# - Blocking function should be prefixed with =wait-on-=.
